answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with slashable stake bonds that vest slowly, like a garden that only yields after tending. Each identity locks a bond in a public registry; if peers prove misconduct, part of it is slashed and paid to honest verifiers. Flooding the network then requires a rising tide of locked capital per fake, not cheap key generation, while one honest agent pays only once. Each bond is also tied to a unique work-history record, a plume of verifiable completed tasks that cannot be copied without redoing the work, so every fake must be separately funded and earned.
